card.name: VSA-A and VSA-B
card.role: the two arrays that hold both copies of every protected disk

def.what: A virtual storage appliance, PowerStore software running inside two virtual machines instead of dedicated hardware.
def.creator: Installed by the storage administrator when the lab was built.
def.reader: The Dell CSI driver over iSCSI, and the lab operator over HTTPS and SSH.
def.where: VSA-A beside spoke-0, VSA-B beside spoke-1, one per site.
def.analogy: Two branch warehouses that each keep a copy of every parcel.

card.name: VSA-A-A, VSA-A-B, VSA-B-A, VSA-B-B
card.role: the two halves of each array, either of which can serve input and output

def.what: One of the two controller virtual machines inside an appliance, called Node A and Node B.
def.creator: Created with the appliance, as two virtual machines on an ESXi host.
def.reader: The other node through the cluster service, and the operator through management.
def.where: Each array has one Node A and one Node B, for example VSA-A-A and VSA-A-B.
def.analogy: Two engines on one aircraft. Either can fly it, and you want both.

card.name: appliance cluster service
card.role: the software that keeps the two nodes acting as one array

def.what: The layer that coordinates the two nodes, decides which one owns a volume, and keeps their view of the data identical.
def.creator: Started by the appliance itself at boot.
def.reader: Both nodes, and the array event log, which reports every state change.
def.where: Inside each appliance, shared by its Node A and Node B.
def.analogy: A referee between two players who must never both grab the ball.

card.name: multipathd and multipath
card.role: the path manager that chooses which physical path to a disk to use

def.what: A service that presents one disk over several physical paths and retries a failed path instead of failing the disk.
def.creator: Started by the node operating system.
def.reader: The kernel device-mapper multipath layer, and anything that issues disk input and output.
def.where: On every array node, for example VSA-A-A.
def.analogy: A courier who knows three routes to the same address.

card.name: khungtaskd and kdump
card.role: the kernel check that panics a node whose task is stuck, and the crash dump after it

def.what: khungtaskd is a kernel thread that reports any task blocked for more than 120 seconds. kdump writes memory to disk after the panic.
def.creator: Part of the Linux kernel and the SUSE configuration on the node.
def.reader: The kernel itself, and the operator reading the serial console.
def.where: On every array node, for example VSA-B-A.
def.analogy: A smoke alarm that also photographs the room.

card.name: PowerStore replication session
card.role: one copy job per volume, between the two arrays

def.what: The array-side object that copies changed blocks for one volume from one array to the other on a schedule.
def.creator: Created when replication is configured, here through the Dell CSI driver and csi-addons.
def.reader: Both arrays, and the Dell CSI driver when it reports status.
def.where: On the source array, named for its volume, for example csivol-ec5862ac71.
def.analogy: A scheduled courier run with a manifest.

card.name: worker initiator sessions
card.role: the login a cluster worker holds to each array node

def.what: A registered iSCSI or NVMe initiator, one per worker node, holding a session to each array node.
def.creator: The worker storage configuration, when it logs in to the array.
def.reader: The array, which counts active sessions per initiator.
def.where: On both arrays, listed per worker.
def.analogy: Two phone lines to the same office, one per receptionist.

card.name: stop reason 351
card.role: the array label for the second node stop

def.what: A numeric stop reason the appliance writes when it changes a node stop type. The log line reads, node stop type was changed from stopped to none, stop reason is 351.
def.creator: The appliance cluster service.
def.reader: The array event log, and Dell support.
def.where: In the event log of each array.
def.analogy: A code on a maintenance ticket that only the manufacturer can decode.
